statement: The valid inequality ||p_Q||_infinity <= sup_b ||p_{Q3|Qrest=b}||_infinity cannot yield a universal proof because the right side is unbounded over admissible target instances.
construction: Independent X1,X3,X4 uniform[0,1]; X2 density indicator of m separated intervals [10k,10k+1/m]. With S=(X1+X2)/sqrt(2), D=(X1-X2)/sqrt(2), Q3=D^2+X3^2-X4^2 and Qrest=S^2, the full Q is diagonal X1^2+X2^2+X3^2-X4^2 and hence has density <=pi.
exact_bound: At b_m=1/(2m^2), p_{Q3|Qrest=b_m}(0) >= 0.5*(log(sqrt(2)m)+1), so sup_b ||p_{Q3|Qrest=b}||_infinity diverges.
mechanism: Worst scalar conditioning squeezes the D core direction to O(1/m), exposing the logarithmic singularity of the opposite-sign pair X3^2-X4^2. The averaging shift over Qrest is essential smoothing and is discarded by the supremum.
concurrent_reconciliation: account03/B18 independently refuted full-vector conditional moments; B16's scalar-Qrest correction is a strictly later target and shows the replacement worst-condition M also fails.
replacement_obligation: Control the shifted mixture E[p_{Q3|Qrest}(t-Qrest)] directly or perform product-preserving aggregation before worst-case conditioning; do not use a uniform sup_b conditional-core bound.
